# M3-13: get_category_decisions

- Milestone: M3
- Branch / worktree: `t/M3-13`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M3-13`
- Depends on: M3-1a
- Touches (exclusive while running): mcp/ (new file `tools_decisions*.go`)
- Plan refs: §4 read tools, R6c, R9; the M2-4 brief's `register` note
- YNAB access: none
- Deploy: no (smoke: none; ships in M3-17)

## Goal
Either user can ask, from an AI client, why a transaction got its category.

## Scope
- Register `get_category_decisions(txn)` with `register(auth.ScopeMCP, ...)` from an `init` in the new file. The `Response[T]` wrapper adds freshness.
- Return the decision history for the active plan: category, confidence, runner-up, method, model, mode, outcome, created_at. Include `second_opinion` when present.
- Use `badRequest` for malformed input. An unknown or undecided transaction returns an empty list with freshness, not an error.
- Follow the id conventions of the existing transaction tools.

## Out of scope
- Write tools, `audit_transactions` (M5).

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Fixture test: superseded decisions appear in order, newest first.
- [ ] Test: another plan's decisions never appear.
- [ ] Test: an undecided transaction returns empty with freshness; malformed input gets the `badRequest` text.
- [ ] Test: the tool needs a valid token (same harness as the existing tools).
- [ ] go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... green

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - `mcp/tools_decisions.go`: new `get_category_decisions` tool, registered with `register(finauth.ScopeMCP, ...)` from `init`. Reads `store.DecisionHistory` for `o.PlanID` and reverses it to newest first.
  - `mcp/tools_decisions_test.go`: fixture tests through the real MCP client and handler.
  - No store, migration or YNAB changes.
- Acceptance:
  - Superseded decisions in order, newest first: pass, `go test ./mcp -run TestCategoryDecisions_NewestFirstWithSuperseded` (includes a same-timestamp tie). Fails when the reverse is removed.
  - Another plan's decisions never appear: pass, `go test ./mcp -run TestCategoryDecisions_OnlyActivePlan` (same txn id in both plans, and an id only in the other plan). Fails when the plan id is changed.
  - Undecided returns empty with freshness; malformed gets the `badRequest` text: pass, `go test ./mcp -run 'TestCategoryDecisions_(UndecidedIsEmptyWithFreshness|MalformedInput|MissingArgument)'`.
  - Needs a valid token: pass, `go test ./mcp -run TestCategoryDecisions_NeedsValidToken` (a real `tools/call` gets 401 with no or bad token, 403 with the wrong scope, and no decision in the body).
  - `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...`: pass.
- Deviations from brief:
  - The argument is `transaction_id`, not `txn`, matching the field `query_transactions` returns.
  - The response also carries `category_id` beside `category` (as `query_transactions` does) and echoes `transaction_id`. `features` and the policy and candidates hashes are left out.
  - The brief doesn't define "malformed". Ids stay opaque (no UUID check, as in the existing tools); empty, over 128 bytes, or containing whitespace or control characters is refused. A missing argument is refused earlier by the SDK's schema check, with its own text rather than the `badRequest` text.
